lessons.title: Neural networks
lessons.subtitle: Week 13: Inside modern AI systems
lessons.body:
A neural network combines layers of mathematical transformations with learned parameters. The term neuron describes a computational unit, not a human brain cell.

Offline practice: Draw a simplified input-layer-output diagram and label it as a conceptual illustration. Write your reasoning before looking at the quiz answers. Record one limitation or uncertainty. You can use paper or local notes; an online AI tool is optional.

Recap: explain yesterday’s key idea from memory, then check your notes. After a break, start with this recap and the first small step of today’s activity.

Complete all three quiz questions before moving on.
takeaways: A neural network combines layers of mathematical transformations with learned parameters. The term neuron describes a computational unit, not a human brain cell.
Apply the idea through the offline activity.
Keep reasoning, evidence, and limitations with your artifact.

lessons.title: Embeddings
lessons.subtitle: Week 13: Inside modern AI systems
lessons.body:
An embedding represents an item as numbers used to capture useful relationships. Similar positions can support comparison, but do not guarantee identical meaning.

Offline practice: Arrange fictional words on paper by similarity and explain why your sketch is not a trained embedding. Write your reasoning before looking at the quiz answers. Record one limitation or uncertainty. You can use paper or local notes; an online AI tool is optional.

lessons.title: Attention
lessons.subtitle: Week 13: Inside modern AI systems
lessons.body:
Attention mechanisms let a model weight relationships between parts of an input. Attention is a mathematical operation, not evidence of awareness or human understanding.

lessons.title: Retrieval-supported generation
lessons.subtitle: Week 13: Inside modern AI systems
lessons.body:
Retrieval-supported generation supplies relevant documents for an answer. It can improve grounding, but retrieval errors and unsupported generated claims still need checks.

Offline practice: Design a workflow that selects a course note before drafting an answer and then verifies the answer. Write your reasoning before looking at the quiz answers. Record one limitation or uncertainty. You can use paper or local notes; an online AI tool is optional.

Recap: explain yesterday’s key idea from memory, then check your notes. After a break, start with this recap and the first small step of today’s activity.

Complete all three quiz questions before moving on.

Apply the idea through the offline activity.

lessons.title: Fine-tuning and choosing tools
lessons.subtitle: Week 13: Inside modern AI systems
lessons.body:
Fine-tuning adapts a pretrained model using additional training. Prompting, retrieval, and fine-tuning are different approaches; training is not always necessary.

Offline practice: Choose a simple document lookup, a prompt, or additional training for three fictional tasks and justify the simplest suitable option. Write your reasoning before looking at the quiz answers. Record one limitation or uncertainty. You can use paper or local notes; an online AI tool is optional.

Recap: explain yesterday’s key idea from memory, then check your notes. After a break, start with this recap and the first small step of today’s activity.

Complete all three quiz questions before moving on.

Weekly completion task: save this week’s practice artifact. Confirm four steps: explain a key idea (recap); complete the practice activity (practice); record what you would verify and where (plan); show your artifact and explain one improvement (demonstrate).
takeaways: Fine-tuning adapts a pretrained model using additional training. Prompting, retrieval, and fine-tuning are different approaches; training is not always necessary.
Apply the idea through the offline activity.
Keep reasoning, evidence, and limitations with your artifact.
